subject: Nomad: tiling + fallback GPU plan for long-context inference

Subject: Sizing question: long-context inference (Nomad POC)

Hi Naomi,

Quick background: we're running a POC that needs to do 1.5k qps of short-chat (avg 64 tokens) plus a smaller set of long-context retrieval+generation calls (avg 2048 tokens, heavy KV cache use) for a fraction of customers.

We wanted some input on which Dedicated GPU SKU makes sense for a committed pool (H100 vs A100 vs L4) given:
- memory pressure from 2k+ sequence windows on a subset of requests
- need for predictable latency on the short-chat path
- wanting a fallthrough option that keeps throughput during heavy long-context spikes

Can you recommend a conservative fleet plan and anything we should expect for packing/tiling? Also, can you share a short checklist we can hand to Procurement?

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Chen
Head of Platform
Nomad.ai

Subject: Re: Sizing question: long-context inference (Nomad POC)

Hi Sara — thanks for the rundown. Looping in Rishi and Karthik for the GPU-level tradeoffs and an ops-friendly plan. I attached a short cheatsheet that walks through tiling/packing basics.

High-level callouts up front:
- H100 (80GB) is the simplest single-node answer for sustained long-context inference (2k+ tokens) without aggressive model sharding. Best for predictable latency on those long requests.
- A100 (40GB) is cost-efficient for high-throughput short-chat; requires more aggressive tiling/sharding for the long requests and will increase engineering complexity (TP/PP and KV cache orchestration).
- L4 (24GB-ish) is cheapest per-GPU and good as a burst/fallback for short-chat, but not suitable to serve the 2k token workload except with heavy batching and a lot of sequence-splitting which can increase latency and harm quality.

Questions for the sizing calc:
1) expected percent of traffic that is long-context vs short-chat (approx)
2) SLOs (p50/p95 target latencies) for both paths
3) tolerance for quality degradation if we do sequence-splitting or context window trimming

I'll hand off to Rishi for specifics and a recommended fleet mix.

—Naomi

Attachment: redwood-tiling-cheatsheet.pdf (PDF, 1 page)

Sara / team — quick technical note with concrete guidance. Replying inline below: 

On 2028-05-19 Naomi wrote: 
> High-level callouts up front:
> - H100 (80GB) is the simplest single-node answer for sustained long-context inference (2k+ tokens) without aggressive model sharding. Best for predictable latency on those long requests.

Agree. To add some numbers and operational signals:
- H100 (80GB): realistic slot sizing for a 2k token Llama-style 70B variant (fp16 / q4f16-like runs) is ~1-2 concurrent requests per GPU if you need <300ms p95 on long requests. If throughput higher, expect to shard or use tensor-model parallelism which increases slot complexity.
- A100 (40GB): you can tile 2-3 short-chat instances per GPU easily for 64-token workloads. For long-context 2k tokens, you likely need sequence-slicing or offload to multi-GPU (2x A100) which raises tail latency and cross-device comms. Operationally A100 is our price/perf sweet spot for majority short-chat traffic.
- L4 (24GB): excellent for stateless short-chat and embedding endpoints; not recommended as primary for long-context. Use L4 for a burst/bastion pool to absorb sudden spikes on short-chat with autoscale policies and quick fallback routing.

Recommended conservative fleet mix (initial committed pool):
- 40% H100 (reserved seats): sized to cover steady-state long-context demand + warm cache headroom
- 45% A100: primary short-chat capacity; good packing for high qps with predictable per-token cost
- 15% L4: burst layer for short-chat overshoot and low-cost dev/preview traffic

Key operational notes:
- KV cache warmup: long-context benefit grows dramatically after warm cache; plan steady warmup windows and allocate warm slots for top 10% customers to prevent cold-start slowness.
- Canary + fallback: route by policy — primary model on H100 for long requests; fallback to A100-larger-batch or L4-bursted path with an explicit quality fallback tag. Implement automatic routing thresholds (p95 latency or queue depth) to trigger fallbacks.
- Autoscaling headroom: reserve ~20% buffer of committed H100 capacity for cache warmups and regression safety.
- Packing heuristics: favor packing many 64-token requests into A100 continuous-batching slots; use preemptible L4s only for non-SLA preview traffic.

If you share traffic mix numbers I can produce a quick per-hour slot count and estimate committed GPUs + expected excess burst.

—Rishi

- SLOs: short-chat p95 < 150ms, long-context p95 < 700ms (we can compromise on p99 for long requests)

Procurement: looping you in. We would prefer a starting committed pool and an option to burst for 6 months while we ramp. Can you attach a template PO/contract language and the SKU matrix so we can map internal approvals?

Sara / Procurement team — attaching a short dedicated proposal and SKU matrix for internal mapping. Summary recommendation based on your stated mix and SLOs: 

1) Committed pool (initial 6-month):
   - 18 H100 nodes (reserved) — covers steady long-context concurrent slots with ~20% warmheadroom
   - 20 A100 nodes — primary short-chat throughput; continuous-batching and packing expected to meet p95 <150ms
   - 6 L4 nodes — burst layer for short-chat spikes and can be used for dev/preview workloads

2) Canary & fallback plan:
   - Start canary with 10% of traffic (by route) on the proposed mapping. Measure p95/p99 and token cost delta.
   - Fallback policy: if H100 p95 > 700ms OR queue depth > 80% for >30s, route long requests to a 2-A100-shard path (best-effort) and set client-facing degradation header.

3) Ops checklist for Procurement (short):
   - Contract: 6-month reserved commit with monthly reviewed burst credits
   - Term: define burst credit caps and overage pricing for L4/A100 usage
   - Audit: include telemetry access (token-level cost, p95 by route) and a one-week ramp window before full production cutover

Next steps: procurement — please review attached PO template (nomad-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf) and the SKU matrix. Rishi / Karthik / Monica will prepare an hour-long ops call next week to walk through warmup and packing rules.

Thanks — we can iterate asap.

—Naomi

Attachments: nomad-dedicated-proposal-v1.pdf (PDF, 4 pages); sku-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 2 sheets)
